children: A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after an AI and chip sell-off pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory and drove traders into defensive shares.

Tech selling deepened as Anthropic fell more than 10% a day after its Nasdaq debut while Nvidia slid over 7% and AMD dropped 11%, leaving the Nasdaq down more than 3%, CNBC data showed. Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned in remarks covered by CNBC against delaying rate hikes.

Steady grocery demand from the previous session reinforced the bid after Walmart's earnings results showed Q3 revenue up 5.2% to $188.8 billion and a raised outlook, with CFO John David Rainey citing mid-single-digit U.S. grocery growth on the call.

When growth valuations compress alongside rate-hike fears, capital rotates to household and grocery names with steadier cash flows. Packaged food's lead over big-box retailers suggests investors are favoring cheaper defensives with room to rebound rather than paying up for crowded retail leaders.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Shelf-stable food company J. M. Smucker jumped 2.7%. Is now the time to buy J. M. Smucker?

Spectrum Brands’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 7 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Spectrum Brands is up 33.5% since the beginning of the year, but at $80.18 per share, it is still trading 12.4% below its 52-week high of $91.57 from November 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Spectrum Brands’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $753.81.
